spec.description: Programmable-resolution (9 to 12-bit) 1-Wire digital thermometer measuring -55C to +125C with +/-0.5C accuracy from -10C to +85C. Each device carries a unique 64-bit ROM code so many sensors can share one data line, and it can be powered either from VDD or parasitically from the data line.
spec.logic_voltage: DQ: -0.3V to +5.5V; VIH min 2.2V (local power) or 3.0V (parasite power), VIL max 0.8V; compatible with 3.3V ESP32 I/O when VDD = 3V3

pins.note: TO-92 pin 1 / SOIC pin 5. Must not float while VDD is supplied (p.3).
TO-92 pin 2 / SOIC pin 4. Open-drain 1-Wire data line; requires an external 4.7k pull-up resistor from DQ to 3V3 (p.4 Fig.3, p.10). ESP32 toggles between driving LOW and INPUT (released).
TO-92 pin 3 / SOIC pin 3. External supply 3.0V-5.5V; use 3V3 so DQ logic levels match the ESP32. For parasite-power mode tie VDD to GND instead (p.2, p.3).

init_sequence.value: DQ low >= 480 us, release, expect presence pulse
init_sequence.purpose: Initialization sequence that begins every 1-Wire transaction; presence pulse confirms a DS18B20 is on the bus
Read the 64-bit ROM: family code 0x28, 48-bit serial number, 8-bit CRC (single device on the bus only)
Address the single DS18B20 without sending its 64-bit ROM code
Read one bit: 0 = parasite powered (strong pull-up needed during conversion), 1 = externally powered
Write Scratchpad: set alarm triggers (unused) and configuration register R1=R0=1 for 12-bit resolution (0.0625C, 750 ms conversion). All 3 bytes must be written before a reset.

warnings: DQ is open-drain and REQUIRES an external ~4.7k (approx. 5k) pull-up resistor to 3V3; without it there is no presence pulse and no communication (p.4, p.10).
Power VDD from 3V3, not 5V: DQ idle level equals the pull-up supply, and the ESP32 GPIO is not 5V tolerant. The DS18B20 itself works from 3.0V to 5.5V (p.24).

If you use parasite power (VDD tied to GND), the master must drive DQ strongly high within 10 us after Convert T for > 750 ms and after Copy Scratchpad for >= 10 ms; the datasheet recommends a MOSFET strong pull-up. The sketch drives the GPIO high which is adequate for a single sensor. Parasite power is not recommended above 100 C (p.3, p.19).
12-bit conversion takes up to 750 ms (9-bit: 93.75 ms). No other bus activity is allowed during a parasite-powered conversion (p.9, p.19).
A reading of 0x0550 (+85 C) is the power-on reset value and indicates the conversion did not complete (p.5).

The bit-banged 1-Wire timing is microsecond-critical; the driver disables interrupts around each time slot. Keep the DQ wire short (or reduce pull-up value for long runs) to keep the rise time within the 15 us read window (p.19, p.21).
Skip ROM (0xCC) and Read ROM (0x33) are only valid with ONE DS18B20 on the bus; for multiple sensors use Search ROM (0xF0) and Match ROM (0x55) with each 64-bit ROM code (p.11).
Do not copy the scratchpad to EEPROM (0x48) every boot; the EEPROM is rated for 50,000 writes (p.8, p.24). This sketch only writes the volatile scratchpad.
Accuracy is +/-0.5 C only from -10 C to +85 C; +/-2 C over the full -55 C to +125 C range (p.24).
GPIO16 is a general-purpose pin on the ESP32 DevKit; if you move DQ, avoid input-only pins GPIO34-39 (cannot drive low), GPIO6-11 (flash) and strapping pins 0, 2, 5, 12, 15.
